negative_findings.description: No documented public REST API for Věstník veřejných zakázek or NEN was found. The only structured route surfaced is the ISVZ OpenData section (isvz.nipez.cz/opendata) plus a methodological help PDF, and the NIPEZ 'Registr veřejných zakázek' documentation describing data structures for inter-tool exchange rather than an open developer endpoint.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in cs and en returned portal and documentation pages, no API reference. Bulk open data appears to be the intended machine route; endpoint shapes and update cadence remain unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for this cell will likely rest on bulk open-data pulls plus HTML crawling, not on a clean API — this materially changes effort estimates and freshness expectations.

negative_findings.description: Commercial banks operating in CZ (ČSOB, KB, Česká spořitelna, etc.) are not contracting authorities under zák. 134/2016 Sb. for their ordinary commercial buying, so their vendor selections for payment infrastructure do not appear in VVZ/NEN. Searches for bank-side tender publication in this cell surfaced only the public-sector institutions (ČNB, NRB) and state bodies.
negative_findings.result_summary: No legally mandated CZ notice channel found for private-bank procurement of payment terminals or acquiring technology.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The A2 procurement workstream can only cover the public/state-financial slice of the CZ banking-and-payments demand side; private-bank vendor selection must be covered by other workstreams (vendor announcements, press, references).

negative_findings.description: Veřejné zakázky malého rozsahu (small-scale contracts, below the statutory thresholds) carry no VVZ publication duty and may appear only on an individual authority's profil zadavatele — or nowhere at all beyond the later contract entry in Registr smluv.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed structurally from the publication-duty framing on portal-vz.cz and from Gemin being described as used for small-scale contracts; no central register of small-scale banking/payment purchases was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Individual terminal purchases, payment-gateway subscriptions and small integrations — the high-frequency, low-value layer most indicative of day-to-day vendor share — are systematically invisible in the headline register.

negative_findings.description: No consolidated public list of certified electronic tools (certifikované elektronické nástroje per vyhláška 260/2016 Sb.) and their operators was located during this pass; the e-tool landscape had to be assembled by snowballing individual vendors (E-ZAK, Tender Arena, Gemin, vhodne-uverejneni, e-zakazky).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned vendor sites and individual authority profiles, not an authoritative registry page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without the authoritative certified-tool list, host coverage is assembled ad hoc and may miss whole platforms, silently under-covering some contracting authorities.

negative_findings.description: Two parallel VVZ hostnames were observed in results — vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz and vvz.nipez.cz (plus cdz.vvz.nipez.cz). Which is currently canonical, and whether one merely redirects, was not established; no fetch was performed to adjudicate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both appear in current search results with live-looking content; relationship unresolved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pointing a collector at the non-canonical host risks silent staleness or duplication; this must be resolved by the deterministic verification pass before collection is configured.

negative_findings.description: No search in this pass surfaced an actual live TED notice for a Czech banking or payment-services contract (CPV 66110000 / 66172000). Web search returned portal and aggregator pages, not notice records.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero concrete CZ finance-CPV notice URLs obtained. This is a limitation of general web search against TED, whose notice pages are rendered client-side and poorly indexed — not evidence that such notices are absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that general web search is the wrong instrument for this cell; the TED Search API with an explicit country+CPV expert query is the only reliable retrieval path, and should be treated as a required build step rather than an optimisation.

negative_findings.description: SIMAP no longer exists as an independent portal; its content has been folded into ted.europa.eu/en/simap/*.
negative_findings.result_summary: The seed brief's 'SIMAP' target resolves to TED sub-pages. One search result additionally mis-glossed SIMAP as an Italian system, which is wrong for this context (EU SIMAP = Système d'information pour les marchés publics).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the pipeline from being pointed at a decommissioned host, and flags that low-quality glossary sites will contaminate any automated definition-gathering step.

negative_findings.description: The widely cited TED-CSV dataset path (data.europa.eu/euodp/en/data/dataset/ted-csv) is a legacy EUODP URL.
negative_findings.result_summary: Referenced repeatedly in secondary sources but not confirmed live in this pass; EUODP has been merged into data.europa.eu and legacy paths commonly redirect or 404.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A pipeline hard-coding the legacy path could silently break. The dataset should be re-located on the current data.europa.eu catalogue before use.

negative_findings.description: Legacy TED FTP bulk access (ftp://ted.europa.eu, guest/guest) is cited by third-party sources but its current availability is unknown.
negative_findings.result_summary: Mentioned in aggregated search output; plain FTP is widely being retired across EU services and was not independently confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical backfill plans should not depend on FTP; budget for the Open Data Service / bulk XML packages instead.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching was performed and was productive (VVZ/NIPEZ, portal-vz.cz, dotaceEU seznam operací, NPO/MMR rules, data.gov.cz all surfaced only via cs queries).
negative_findings.result_summary: Four of six searches used Czech terms. English-only searching would have missed the entire national eSender and EU-funds transparency layer.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Validates the mandatory local-language rule for this cell and gives a reusable cs glossary for later runs.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-language TED-side vocabulary was found for payment-industry specifics (acquiring, card personalisation, ATM outsourcing) as they appear in eForms subject fields.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword recall for CZ notices will be weak until real cs notice titles are harvested and mined for the actual phrasing buyers use.

negative_findings.description: No banking- or payments-specific ÚOHS 'sborník rozhodnutí' was found. The published sectoral digests cover healthcare (01/2021–06/2024) and telecommunications/telematics (01/2021–12/2023), plus construction, but not financial services.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector digests exist but none for banking/payments; banking-related rulings must be found by keyword search across the general decision collection.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must rely on full-text keyword retrieval with a well-built Czech glossary rather than a curated sector feed, raising both recall risk and noise.

negative_findings.description: No official ÚOHS machine API for the decision collection was identified in searches; the accessible structured route is the third-party Hlídač státu dataset/API, whose original-source field points at the legacy uohs.cz path.
negative_findings.result_summary: Official access appears to be HTML search form plus per-decision PDFs only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection depends either on scraping a legacy search form or on an NGO intermediary, creating a single point of failure and a lag/completeness risk.

negative_findings.description: Both ÚOOÚ (uoou.cz → uoou.gov.cz) and Státní pokladna (statnipokladna.cz → statnipokladna.gov.cz) appear mid-migration, with old and new URLs both circulating in search results. ÚOHS likewise moved from uohs.cz to uohs.gov.cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Legacy URLs still returned by search engines; not verified whether they redirect or 404.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Stored URLs will rot; a 404 on a legacy path must be treated as 'moved', not 'dead source'. Collectors should normalise to the .gov.cz hosts and re-resolve legacy links.

negative_findings.description: ČNB JERRS is served from a legacy Oracle web portal with session/login-style URL parameters (JERRS.WEB45.LOGIN_A?p_lang=cz&p_err=8) rather than clean permalinks.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-weighting ÚOOÚ in the collection plan; it is best used as vendor/technology intelligence and compliance-driven demand signal, not as a tender source.

negative_findings.description: 'Bidmall' was searched in both English and a Czech-context query ('bidmall tender', 'Bidmall vyhledávač veřejných zakázek'). negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the platform-indexing strategy of this cell yields public-sector and state-owned buyers well, but almost nothing for commercial banks — private-sector RFP intelligence must come from other cells (vendor references, press, contract register).

Market-share figures for PVU/E-ZAK/Tender arena/profilzadavatele.cz come from a vendor-adjacent blog (elektronizace-zakazek.cz, QCM) and third-party summaries, not an official register.

negative_findings.description: 'Tender market' from the seed list was not resolved to a specific CZ platform in the searches run; it may be a generic phrase or a Slovak/regional product rather than a distinct Czech certified tool. Not present in the MMR certified-tool table fetched.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language search for an explicit bank vacancy naming core-banking migration ('projektový manažer migrace jádrového systému', Praha) returned only generic job-board landing pages, no live matching posting.

negative_findings.description: No stable Czech term was confirmed for the role 'vendor manager' in a banking context; searches on 'manažer dodavatelů' / 'nákup' returned no bank-specific postings.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword lists for automated monitoring must be bilingual and generous ('vendor manager', 'supplier manager', 'manažer dodavatelů', 'specialista nákupu', 'procurement specialist') or recall will be poor.

negative_findings.result_summary: Only landing/aggregate pages were reachable via search; no listing content could be enumerated openly. Not verified as dead, only as restricted.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language search for 2026 bank executive appointments in IT/cards ('jmenován', 'novým ředitelem') returned mostly ČNB and Česká pošta personnel news, no commercial-bank payments/IT appointment.
negative_findings.result_summary: Role-change news for commercial banks is dispersed across trade press and LinkedIn rather than concentrated in a searchable feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A dedicated appointments watchlist (bankovnictvionline.cz, MediaGuru, ManagementNews, EduCity personální změny) is needed rather than ad-hoc search.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searches for a cancelled or contested payment-terminal tender criticised by ÚOHS ('tendr na platební terminály zrušen kritika ÚOHS') returned no matching media article. Results were dominated by unrelated ÚOHS cases (Prague Metro D, football TV rights) and general ÚOHS pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech media article located specifically on a cancelled payment-terminal tender; only an indirect mention that ČSOB was found not to meet certain acquirer tender-documentation requirements (payment applications for some terminal types, EMV readers) appeared in search summaries, and this was NOT verified against a primary document.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payment-terminal/acquiring tenders may be too small or too commercially routine for Czech media, meaning A2 coverage for terminals must lean on ÚOHS decision collections and the contracts register rather than journalism.

negative_findings.description: Neovlivni.cz, an investigative outlet often cited on Czech procurement/political-business links, did not surface in any of the executed searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search explicitly naming Neovlivní.cz returned only Ekonomický deník and Hlídač státu results; no Neovlivní article or domain confirmation obtained.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The outlet may be dormant, renamed, or deindexed for these queries; its absence is unconfirmed either way and should be re-checked before excluding it from the source register.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for private-bank supplier selections ('banka vysoutěžila zakázku dodavatel IT systém') returned almost exclusively public-sector tenders (ministries, tax administration, building authorities, VZP).
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech media article found reporting a named commercial bank running a competitive IT/payments tender with a disclosed winner and value.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Commercial banks in CZ are not contracting authorities under the procurement act, so their supplier selections are not published and are rarely reported; A2 coverage of private-bank vendor deals must come from vendor press releases, trade press features (Bankovnictví, Computerworld) and personnel/reference signals rather than tender data.

negative_findings.description: Two of the highest-value investigative sources for contested contracts (Deník N, and parts of HN and Týdeník Euro) are behind hard or metered paywalls.
negative_findings.result_summary: Article bodies not retrievable anonymously; only headlines, leads and third-party summaries accessible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Systematic A2 monitoring will require paid subscriptions or a licensed press-clipping service; scraping paywalled text is not an option.

negative_findings.description: Searched for Czech national procurement datasets onboarded into the EU Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS). Results listed TED (2021+) and national datasets for Austria, Germany, Finland and Norway, but no Czech national dataset appeared among them.
negative_findings.result_summary: CZ coverage in PPDS appears to be only via the EU-wide TED layer, i.e. above-threshold notices only; below-threshold Czech contracts are not reachable there.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A scout relying on PPDS alone would systematically miss the below-EU-threshold banking/payments contracts, which in CZ are precisely where many card, terminal and paper-consumables purchases sit. National routes (ISVZ OpenData, NEN profile XML, Registr smluv) remain mandatory.

negative_findings.description: Searched in English for Datlab's tender database API access and pricing. Found the company site, the Digiwhist member page and an Apiary documentation space (digiwhist.docs.apiary.io), but no published pricing, licence terms or self-service API key flow.
negative_findings.result_summary: Datlab commercial access conditions are opaque from open sources; a direct commercial enquiry is required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Datlab is the highest-quality normalised CZ tender/supplier source. Not knowing cost or licence terms blocks a build-vs-buy decision for the A2 collection stack and risks planning around data that may be unaffordable or contractually unusable.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for procurement open data combined with banking terms did not surface any dataset scoped to the banking or payments sector; all CZ procurement datasets found are horizontal (all sectors), sliceable only by CPV code or buyer IČO.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ready-made banking/payments procurement dataset exists for CZ; sector scoping must be constructed by the collector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collection design must own CPV-code and buyer-list curation (e.g. CPV 30/48/66/72 families plus a hand-built list of banks, ČNB, state financial institutions). Without that, sector recall will be driven by keyword luck rather than a defined frame.

negative_findings.description: References to old.vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz appeared only indirectly, via a municipal site's file-download link, while current VVZ content sits under the NIPEZ domains (vvz.nipez.cz, cdz.vvz.nipez.cz). I did not fetch the legacy domain and cannot state whether it resolves.
negative_findings.result_summary: The pre-NIPEZ VVZ domain appears superseded; status unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historic Czech notice URLs captured in older research or link collections are likely to be dead or redirected, so historic reconstruction should route through Wayback CDX prefix queries on the legacy domain rather than assuming live retrieval.

negative_findings.description: There is no established Czech-language term for web-archive infrastructure equivalent to 'CDX API'; searching for archive-based recovery of expired Czech notices had to be conducted in English against Internet Archive documentation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Archive-tooling discovery was English-only by necessity; the Czech national web archive (Webarchiv, NK ČR) was not investigated in this slice.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Webarchiv.cz may hold Czech-domain captures the Internet Archive lacks, particularly for government sites under legal-deposit crawling, so an archive route may be under-covered.

negative_findings.description: None of the five parent groups publishes an open, browsable notice board of live tenders or of awarded framework agreements. Erste Group Procurement publishes only a supplier document pack; KB publishes only supplier terms; SG runs competitions inside a login-gated Sourcing Hub whose self-registration has reportedly been withdrawn; KBC routes everything through formal purchasing documents issued by its Belgian procurement department; RBI publishes only a supplier code of conduct.
negative_findings.result_summary: Group-level A2 (tender/award) collection cannot be notice-driven. It must be reconstructed from policy documents, press releases, counterparty disclosures, vendor case studies and the Czech contract register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design that assumes a scrapeable notice feed for these actors will silently return nothing. Budget must move to indirect and counterparty channels.

negative_findings.description: No public supplier-registration or e-sourcing portal URL was located for Erste Group Procurement, KBC Group, RBI or UniCredit despite targeted en searches. An erstegroupprocurement.com domain is implied by the group's email format as reported by third-party profile aggregators, but I did not reach or confirm any web presence on it.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal endpoints for four of five groups remain unknown; only Société Générale's Sourcing Hub was identified by URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without the portal endpoint we cannot even monitor registration-rule changes, which are the main market-access lever for a challenger vendor.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching using the cell's own vocabulary (centrální nákup, dodavatelský portál, skupinový nákup, mateřská banka, výběrové řízení) returned essentially no group-procurement content: the Česká spořitelna query returned only retail banking pages, and the ČSOB query returned CSR interviews and the English KBC group policy rather than any Czech procurement page. The single productive Czech-language hit was kb.cz/cs/dodavatele.
negative_findings.result_summary: Group-level sourcing is documented almost exclusively in English (and French for SG), even where the buying entity is Czech.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise from the negative side: a cs-only collection strategy would miss the layer where CZ vendor decisions are actually made. It also means cs-language monitoring should be aimed at the CZ subsidiaries' supplier-terms pages, not at group sourcing.

negative_findings.description: A targeted search for which e-sourcing suite (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer) each of Erste, RBI, UniCredit and KBC runs returned only generic vendor-comparison content and no bank-specific implementation evidence.
negative_findings.result_summary: Toolchain attribution for four groups is unresolved. Only SG's own-branded Sourcing Hub and TradeShift (invoicing) and RBI's use of akirolabs for category strategy are evidenced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Knowing the platform tells you the registration path, the notice format and often the public supplier-discovery surface (e.g. Ariba Discovery), so this gap directly blocks a collection route.

negative_findings.description: Erste Group Procurement states it has a Czech subsidiary, but I could not confirm its registered Czech name or IČO; the search returned Czech register portals (ares.cz, rejstrik.penize.cz) and an unrelated Erste Group Immorent ČR s.r.o. entity rather than the procurement company.
negative_findings.result_summary: The CZ contracting entity of Erste's group procurement arm is named but not identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Until it is resolved by IČO, contract-register and filing searches for Erste group-level CZ purchasing cannot be run reliably.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit Services S.C.p.A., the group entity described as providing procurement among its shared services, was merged into UniCredit S.p.A. on 1 October 2022. The unicreditgroup.eu microsite describing it may therefore document a superseded structure.
negative_findings.result_summary: UniCredit's current group-procurement home is not confirmed; the best available page is possibly legacy.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Attributing a CZ vendor decision to a dissolved entity would be an error; the current owner of the sourcing function must be re-established before this source is relied on.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted before planned follow-ups could run: registr smluv queries scoped to Česká spořitelna and Erste Digital, KBC/ČSOB Czech-language supplier pages on csob.cz, group annual-report/CSRD supply-chain disclosures, and Ariba Discovery-style supplier-network surfaces.
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage of this cell is solid on the five parent groups' policy layer but thin on the disclosure-by-obligation layer (annual reports, CSRD/DORA third-party registers).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The unexplored DORA register-of-information angle is potentially the single highest-value A2 route for this cell and remains untested.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, standing publication was found for ČNB's procurement of CERTIS (interbank clearing) components or suppliers. CERTIS surfaced only as a named information system inside ČNB cyber-security/supplier documentation, not as a tendered subject with its own notice trail.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched cs for ČNB + CERTIS + dodavatel/výběrové řízení; hits were the generic E-ZAK ČNB profile and unrelated documents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CERTIS is the core national payment rail; if its supplier arrangements are never openly tendered (in-house or below-threshold RFQ), the market-intel path must shift to registr smluv, NKÚ audits and ČNB annual reports rather than tender monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Below-threshold purchases (veřejné zakázky malého rozsahu, up to CZK 3m for supplies/services at ČNB) and Česká pošta's sector small-scope contracts are awarded under internal rules by RFQ to selected suppliers, with limited or no public advertising.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both ČNB's mandatory-disclosure page and Česká pošta's procurement page state this explicitly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A large share of payment-related pilots and terminal top-ups will never appear as a tender notice; only the signed contract in registr smluv will reveal them, so contract-register monitoring cannot be treated as optional.

negative_findings.description: The state payment-gateway programme is administered by the Ministry of the Interior (contact platebnibrany@mvcr.cz) via a centralised DNS, not by the Ministry of Finance, despite MF being the fiscal owner of state payment rails.
negative_findings.result_summary: platebnibrany.gov.cz and archi.gov.cz describe MV ČR as the DNS administrator; DIA appears in the wider eGovernment portal context.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Monitoring only MF/treasury buyers would miss the single largest recurring channel for public-sector payment-gateway demand; the cell boundary needs an explicit MV ČR / DIA hand-off.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching returned essentially no Czech central-state payment-services notices; EN results were generic TED explainers and commercial tender-aggregator marketing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: EN query on TED + Czech MoF + card acceptance produced no matching CZ notice; only a UK banking-services example.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that Czech-language querying is not optional for this cell and that any EN-only monitoring pipeline would have near-zero recall outside TED's structured fields.

negative_findings.description: The NEN MF profile URL (nen.nipez.cz/profil/mfcr) and the ISVZ open-data URL (isvz.nipez.cz/opendata) were reported in secondary/official text but not independently opened during this pass; NEN paths are known to change form.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded from MF's own procurement page and the ISVZ open-data help PDF reference.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are backbone collection endpoints; the deterministic liveness pass should confirm exact current paths before the pipeline is built on them.

negative_findings.description: Searching in Czech for payments/banking tenders at municipal level did not surface any official portal that full-text searches across all profily zadavatele. VVZ indexes profile URLs and notices, but the small-scale contracts (VZMR) that dominate municipal payment purchases live only on each buyer's own profile.
negative_findings.result_summary: Enumeration-then-crawl (VVZ profile registry as seed) plus the Hlídač státu API are the only viable cross-cutting approaches found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design cannot rely on one query endpoint; it needs a per-platform parser strategy across at least five hosting families (NEN, E-ZAK, Tender arena, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz/profilzadavatele.cz).

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for Czech municipal contactless-transport-payment tender award notices returned only tourist/operator pages and generic tender-alert vendors, no primary notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is unusable as a discovery language for this cell; only cs queries surfaced primary procurement sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms local-language-first collection; English sources are at best corroborating context (Smart Prague, DPP EN pages).

negative_findings.description: Prague's parking payment app market is being opened via a published onboarding process with a fixed 4% distribution fee rather than via a competitive tender, and MPLA support ends 31.12.2025 in favour of a city-run web parking meter.
negative_findings.result_summary: Relevant buying signal exists outside the tender corpus entirely.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A tender-only collection scope would miss how payment providers actually gain access to municipal payment flows; operator/city announcement pages must be tracked alongside profiles.

negative_findings.description: Several canonical profile URLs (tenderarena.cz/profily/HlavniMestoPraha, tenderarena.cz/profily/DPP, uohs.gov.cz decision-collection root) were reported in search results but not fetched by me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence_score; treated as hypotheses pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false 'verified' claims; these are high-value targets that should be checked first.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, curated dataset or portal exists that isolates banking/payment-services contracts within the Czech contract register. Searching 'registr smluv platebni terminaly dodavatel smlouva' returned the register's generic pages and unrelated contracts rather than any sectoral view.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector filtering must be built by us, from free-text subject fields plus a supplier ICO watchlist; no ready-made banking slice was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Implies real engineering effort (keyword + ICO + CPV-style classification) before the register yields a usable banking/payments series, and implies recall risk from inconsistent free-text subjects.

negative_findings.description: The register's exemptions regime — notably the banking-secrecy carve-out discussed in Czech legal commentary, plus redaction of commercially sensitive terms (files named *_RED.PDF) — removes or obscures part of the bank-side contract content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Pricing schedules and some counterparty terms in banking contracts may be redacted or the contract exempt entirely; presence in the register is not proof of full disclosure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any pricing benchmark drawn from these documents must be flagged as a lower bound on visibility, not a complete market picture.

negative_findings.description: The official register publishes bulk monthly XML dumps and publication (write) interfaces, but I found no documented official read/query REST API for ad-hoc searching. Programmatic search appears to require either local ingestion of the dumps or the third-party Hlidac statu API.
negative_findings.result_summary: Official access pattern is bulk-download-and-index; ad-hoc programmatic search depends on a third party.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Creates a dependency: either we run our own index (cost, but full control) or we depend on Hlidac's availability and terms for query-time access.

negative_findings.description: Official documentation states that historical XML dumps are rewritten retroactively when a contract is modified or made inaccessible, and that all versions of a withdrawn contract are removed from historical dumps.
negative_findings.result_summary: The register is not an append-only archive; past snapshots can silently change or lose records.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Longitudinal series can shift under us and disappearances can be mistaken for market changes; we must keep our own timestamped, hashed snapshots and diff them.

negative_findings.description: data.isrs.cz is cited in the official open-data documentation as the dump directory listing, but I did not independently fetch it in this pass. registrysmluv.cz's operator, coverage claim (8.3m contracts) and terms of service were likewise not verified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both recorded with reduced confidence rather than as confirmed live sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids overstating availability of a fallback mirror and of a commercial index whose licence terms could forbid automated collection.

negative_findings.description: The official open-data page states explicitly that the dataset contains personal data within the meaning of GDPR, that the recipient becomes a controller, and that records made inaccessible must be deleted from downstream systems.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk ingestion carries an affirmative data-protection obligation, including honouring retroactive redactions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The collector needs a deletion/reconciliation routine and a documented lawful basis before we ingest at scale — this is a build requirement, not a footnote.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for the Czech contract register returned mostly the register's own pages, Wikipedia and generic legal-dictionary noise; no substantive English analytical coverage of Czech disclosed banking contracts was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is usable for framing and legal context only; all real discovery in this cell must be done in Czech.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that any collector or analyst working this cell needs Czech-language keyword lists; an English-only pipeline would miss essentially everything.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated portal or register exists that isolates 'sectoral/utility contracting entity' contracts for payment or banking services in CZ. Under Act 134/2016 Sb. the concept of 'sektorový zadavatel' was replaced by 'sektorová veřejná zakázka', so the sectoral character is an attribute of an individual notice, not of a separate publication channel.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed via MMR's portal-vz.cz Q&A; sectoral contracts are published in the general Věstník veřejných zakázek and on ordinary buyer profiles.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must filter by buyer IČO + CPV rather than expect a sectoral-specific feed; otherwise sectoral buyers will be systematically missed or double-counted.

negative_findings.description: Searching in English for a Czech Railways ticketing/payment-gateway award notice on TED returned only generic railway-engineering and rolling-stock notices, no payment/ticketing award.
negative_findings.result_summary: EN-language TED searching did not surface the target notice; Czech-language searching on the ČD buyer profile is the more productive route.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms EN-only monitoring is insufficient for this cell — many payment-related sectoral contracts are below EU thresholds or described only in Czech.

negative_findings.description: For water utilities (vodárny a kanalizace), Czech-language searching for procurement of payment collection / card acceptance returned only customer-facing payment-method pages (PVK, OVAK, SčVK, VAK Mladá Boleslav, Vodárna Plzeň), not tenders.
negative_findings.result_summary: No vodárna tender for payment acceptance located in this pass; only descriptions of accepted payment channels (bankovní inkaso, SIPO, QR platba, SAZKA terminals, cards at customer centres).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Many water utilities are majority-private (Veolia/Suez-owned operating companies) and therefore may fall outside the procurement regime entirely, meaning their payment-acceptance sourcing is invisible in tender data and must be inferred from customer pages and the contract register.

negative_findings.description: For several commercial e-tools (Tender Arena, E-ZAKAZKY.CZ, podo.fen.cz, najdivz.cz) the terms of service for automated crawling were not read in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public browsing is stated as possible without registration for Tender Arena, but robots.txt/ToS were not checked for any of these hosts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection could breach ToS; a legal/robots review is required before scheduling crawlers on private profile hosts, whereas VVZ, NEN, TED and smlouvy.gov.cz are safe open-data routes.

negative_findings.description: The historically canonical gazette domain vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz was superseded by vvz.nipez.cz following an operator change in April 2023.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both domains still appear in search results and in older documents; the legacy one should be treated as unverified/legacy rather than dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any monitoring configuration or historical URL set pointing at the old domain must be re-pointed, and archived links may need resolution through the new system.

negative_findings.description: Česká spořitelna (csas.cz) appears to have NO 'pro dodavatele' / supplier section at all. Czech-language searches combining csas.cz with dodavatel, nákup, kodex dodavatele, portál dodavatele, sourcing, and výběrové řízení returned only unrelated client-facing content (e-Faktura, eFactoring, ESG guidance sold to corporate clients) plus third-party pages. The Erste Group Procurement finding explains why: ČS external spend is handled by the group procurement shared service, which has its own Czech subsidiary.
negative_findings.result_summary: No csas.cz supplier/procurement URL identified across four cs and en query variants; the function is confirmed to sit at Erste Group Procurement instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Anyone hunting for a ČS supplier portal will find nothing and may wrongly conclude ČS does not tender. The correct target is the Erste Group Procurement CZ entity, not csas.cz — a routing correction that changes where the whole ČS demand signal is watched.

negative_findings.description: Every csob.cz URL I attempted returned HTTP 500 Internal Server Error — both https://www.csob.cz/dodavatele and the procurement policy PDF at /documents/10710/927640/procurement-politika-vztahu-s-dodavateli-en.pdf, the latter having appeared as a live search result. A uniform 500 across unrelated paths is characteristic of bot defence or edge-layer filtering, not of missing documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: csob.cz: 2/2 fetch attempts returned HTTP 500. Content confirmed to exist via search index and via a Czech third-party interview describing the same policy. Recorded as unverified, NOT dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ČSOB is the largest CZ bank by assets and a core target of this cell. If the collector is a plain HTTP client it will silently fail on the whole csob.cz estate and the bank will look sourceless. The pipeline needs a headless-browser fetch path for this domain.

negative_findings.description: No supplier, procurement, or vendor-onboarding page found for Air Bank, Partners Banka, or Fio banka. Czech-language searching (dodavatelé, nákup, výběrové řízení, dodavatel, spolupráce) returned only retail-product and press content. For Air Bank the nearest artefact is the PPF Group / Home Credit Code of Ethics, which mentions an Air Bank ethics reporting mailbox but says nothing about procurement. Fio banka, as a domestically owned bank with no foreign parent, publishes no supplier instrument at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three of eight target banks yield zero supplier-channel sources in either language.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is intrinsically capped at roughly five of eight banks via web sources. Air Bank/Fio demand signal must be reached by other means (register filings, staff mapping, trade press, direct contact), not by portal monitoring.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia has no locatable CZ supplier/procurement page. Searches in cs and en returned only client-facing material — the Global Transaction Banking country page, a merchant acquiring portal (merchantportal-unicredit-cz.posmansuite.com, which is a POS-merchant service, NOT a supplier portal), the API developer catalogue, and directory entries. A follow-up en search for a UniCredit group-level 'suppliers portal' returned no UniCredit-owned result at all, only generic vendor-portal marketing.
negative_findings.result_summary: No UniCredit CZ or UniCredit Group supplier portal URL established in two targeted searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Risk of a false positive: the merchant portal is superficially portal-shaped and could be miscatalogued as a supplier channel. It is not. UniCredit is currently the weakest-covered systemic bank in this cell.

negative_findings.description: Across all eight target banks I found no instance of a published RFP, tender notice, or award notice on a bank's own site. Supplier-facing publication is uniformly limited to policy artefacts: codes of conduct, general purchase terms, ESG/responsible-purchasing charters. The one confirmed tender mention for a target bank — Česká spořitelna's tender for the sale of a receivables portfolio, reported by Patria — is an asset disposal, i.e. the bank selling, not buying, and so falls outside supplier-side procurement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero buy-side tender or award notices located on any of the eight banks' own channels.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for workstream A2 in CZ: private-bank cells produce policy and process intelligence, never notice-level demand data. Pipelines built to parse award notices will return empty for this cell no matter how well they are tuned.

negative_findings.description: For no target bank could I confirm the named e-sourcing platform through which RFx invitations are actually issued. Leads only: SG references a 'Sourcing Hub' e-sourcing portal (KB's parent) but publishes no entry URL; RBI is documented on akirolabs category management with an ORACLE iProcurement-based e-auction reference in secondary reporting; Erste Group Procurement describes a standardised onboarding process but names no tool; ČSOB is described only as accepting offers electronically. Attempts to tie any bank to Ariba, Jaggaer, Coupa or Ivalua produced no primary evidence.
negative_findings.result_summary: 0/8 banks with a confirmed, named, entry-point-resolved sourcing platform; 3 partial leads, all secondary or unnamed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The sourcing platform is the chokepoint where demand becomes visible to an invited vendor. Not knowing it means the cell can characterise policy but cannot position for invitation. Resolving this is the highest-leverage next step, and it likely requires human/commercial channels rather than web collection.

negative_findings.description: Group-level procurement doctrine that governs Czech sourcing — Erste Group Procurement, KBC group supplier policy, SG responsible sourcing, RBI group code — is published predominantly in English or German. Czech-language equivalents exist only where the local bank republishes them (KB's Czech PDF stack, rb.cz's Czech slug). Erste's general supplier page states country-translated documents exist behind a drop-down, but I could not reach the Czech variant with a non-rendering fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language coverage is good at bank level (KB, Moneta, rb.cz, ČSOB) but thin at the group level that actually decides.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A cs-only collection strategy would miss the layer where CZ sourcing decisions are genuinely made; an en-only strategy would miss the binding local contract terms. Both languages are required, and the Erste country drop-down specifically needs a rendering fetcher.

negative_findings.description: No Czech bank was found listed as a zadavatel (contracting authority) on any Czech e-procurement platform — TENDER ARENA, proebiz/profily.proebiz.com, or JOSEPHINE. Searching these platforms with banking terms returned only platform help documentation and public-sector contracts, including a public-sector 'poptávkové řízení - poskytnutí úvěru' where a bank is the BIDDER, not the buyer.
negative_findings.result_summary: No target bank identified as a buyer on any CZ e-procurement platform.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale empirically: private systemic banks bypass Czech public portals entirely. Also flags an inversion trap — banks appear on these portals frequently as suppliers of credit to public bodies, which must not be mistaken for bank procurement.

negative_findings.description: Searched for a Monet+ press release or reference page naming a Czech bank customer, in Czech ('Monet+ reference česká banka platební řešení tisková zpráva'). No Monet+ own-domain press release or reference page surfaced in results; only a third-party vendor-catalogue profile.
negative_findings.result_summary: Monet+ is confirmed as a CZ digital-identity/payment vendor selling to banks, but no public 'selected by <bank>' artefact was located in this pass. Its own site (monetplus.cz) was not returned by the search engine and remains unchecked.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Monet+ is a named target actor for this cell; absence of a discoverable reference page means its bank wins may be traceable only via bank-side releases, register filings, or trade press.

negative_findings.description: Auriga press-release and press-review sections were searched in English for a Czech bank customer; only product launches (WWS INSIGHT) and generic showcase pages were returned.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Auriga CZ customer reference found. Auriga has no obvious Czech-language publication channel, so a cs-language query had no meaningful local terms to use.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If Auriga has CZ deployments they are undisclosed publicly, meaning ATM-software market share in CZ cannot be inferred from vendor announcements alone.

negative_findings.description: Thales/Gemalto banking-payment press archive searched in en with cs terms appended ('banka karty'). Only non-CZ customer press releases (e.g. Al Rajhi Bank) and generic product pages returned.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech issuer named in Thales card-issuance communications found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card personalisation/issuance awards at CZ banks may be handled by local bureaux rather than announced by the platform vendor — suggests redirecting to CZ card-personalisation bureaux as a source category.

negative_findings.description: Searched for Backbase / Temenos / Fiserv announcements naming Air Bank, Banka CREDITAS or Raiffeisenbank CZ. Results returned only vendor comparison marketing and unrelated Raiffeisen entities.
negative_findings.result_summary: No global core/digital-banking platform vendor announcement naming a Czech bank was located. Query was English-only; a cs equivalent was not run for these vendors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Core-banking replacement at CZ mid-tier banks is a high-value signal; its absence from vendor newsrooms means detection must lean on integrator news (Cleverlance/Trask type) and trade press instead.

negative_findings.description: Printec Czech Republic: searched in Czech for a CZ reference/case-study page ('reference banka samoobslužné technologie'). Search returned the group site, the Slovak country page, company-register mirrors and a Verifone partner listing, but no CZ-specific customer reference page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Printec's CZ customer references are not discoverable via general search; the group site's case-study section was not enumerated in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Printec-type integrators are the cell's central archetype; if their CZ wins are unpublished, the cell's coverage depends disproportionately on OEM (Diebold/NCR) and bank-side announcements.

negative_findings.description: For several queries the top results were aggregators (kurzy.cz, penize.cz, bankovnictvionline.cz, atmmarketplace.com) rather than the vendor's own release, indicating vendor primary sources are weakly indexed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Primary vendor URLs frequently had to be inferred by snowballing from aggregator copies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design should treat aggregators as the discovery layer and vendor sites as the confirmation layer, not the reverse.

negative_findings.description: Czech PSPs and gateways (ComGate, GoPay, Besteron) are private companies and are not contracting authorities; targeted cs queries for 'výběrové řízení', 'poptávkové řízení' and 'dodavatel' on these actors returned only merchant-facing marketing and gateway-comparison content, no procurement notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: No supplier-selection notices found on or about ComGate/GoPay; only product comparison pages and integration docs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell hypothesis: payments-side vendor selection in CZ is invisible to public registers and must be inferred from press releases, corporate filings and integration/changelog evidence.

negative_findings.description: Besteron (SK-origin gateway active in CZ) did not surface in any of the cs searches run; no corporate press or partner page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero results attributable to Besteron.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A named cell actor is currently uncovered; its partner/bank relationships are unmapped.

negative_findings.description: No Visa Czech-language newsroom or CZ-specific Visa press index was located; searches surfaced only Mastercard's cs-cz newsroom. Visa CZ announcements appear to route through the pan-European English newsroom or partner banks' press pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Mastercard has a cs-cz release index; Visa equivalent not found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Half the card-scheme rule-setter coverage for the cell lacks a local-language primary channel and must be reached indirectly.

negative_findings.description: No CERTIS- or instant-payments-specific supplier/tender document was found via search; ČNB pages describe rules and participants but searches did not reach an individual CERTIS technology contract notice.
negative_findings.result_summary: CERTIS supplier identity not established from open search in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The core national rail's vendor chain remains unmapped; requires direct enumeration of ezak.cnb.cz and registr smluv rather than search engines.

negative_findings.description: SBK's web presence is split across two domains (bankovnikarty.cz and bankovni-karty.cz) with an apparently dated structure; which is canonical and whether member-only material exists was not established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two candidate domains, canonical one unresolved; no fetch attempted to verify.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Risk of collecting from a stale mirror and missing current member/vendor lists.

negative_findings.description: CACIO (Czech Association of IT Managers, ~101 members) does not appear to publish a member directory on the open web; searches in cs returned only 'o nás', event and magazine pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: No public roster located; membership likely disclosed only internally.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes a potential decision-maker map for bank IT buying; substitute is event programmes, which are slower and partial.

negative_findings.description: Asociace poskytovatelů platebních služeb ČR (ASPPS, IČO 04387783) — searches in cs returned registry records (ARES, obchodní rejstřík mirrors) and the aspps.eu homepage, but no membership page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association exists and is active, membership composition unknown from surface search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the most topically precise payments-provider body in the cell; without its roster the PSP-side buyer map relies on ČNB registers and the fintech association instead.

negative_findings.description: Hospodářská komora ČR: no single national member/supplier catalogue was located. Search surfaced only a niche database (authorised lift firms) and regional chamber member pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Chamber membership appears fragmented across ~57 OHK sites and ~140 industry associations.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection cost for chamber-derived supplier discovery is far higher than a single scrape; must be planned as a multi-site crawl.

negative_findings.description: Svaz měst a obcí ČR national site did not surface an open itemised list of member municipalities; only a regional union (SMOJK) and commercial mayor databases (expanzo, Regionservis) appeared.
negative_findings.result_summary: National municipal membership roster not found on the open web.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Municipal buyers must be enumerated from the official municipality register instead of association membership, changing how buyer coverage is measured.

negative_findings.description: cbaonline.cz returned a 'Stránka nenalezena' 404 for the guessed path /o-nas/clenove-cba, while /clenove resolved with the member list. Search indexes also carry www.cbaonline.cz/o-nas/clenove.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple competing member-page paths; guessed paths 404. Not evidence the source is dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors must discover the members link from site navigation each run rather than hardcoding a path, or coverage will silently drop to zero.

negative_findings.description: None of the associations examined (ČBA, ČLFA, ICT UNIE, SBK, Czech Fintech Association, APEK) surfaced a dedicated tender/procurement notice section of their own within this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Associations in this cell act as actor-map pointers, not as tender publishers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell should be scored on pointer/actor-mapping value; actual A2 notices must come from the procurement-portal cells, with association rosters used for entity resolution.

negative_findings.description: 'AFI' from the cell brief is ambiguous in Czech: searches returned afi.cz (a consultancy), AFIZ (Asociace finančních zprostředkovatelů, now merged into ČASF), AFP ČR (financial advisers) and CzGBC noise — no payments/fintech body named AFI was confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: No fintech/payments association reliably identified under the acronym AFI.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Flags a noisy term for the glossary; downstream runs should search ČASF/AFIZ explicitly instead of 'AFI'.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief's 'ČSOB/AKAT lists' conflates a commercial bank (ČSOB) with the capital-market association AKAT. ČSOB is a member entity (of ČBA, SBK, SPIR), not a list publisher; AKAT is the association with a member roster.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only AKAT ČR (akatcr.cz) was treated as a list source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a wasted collection target and corrects the actor map for downstream cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Mini-tenders awarded inside dynamic purchasing systems and framework agreements (DNS / rámcové dohody) generally do not generate individual high-visibility notices, yet they are how much CZ public ICT and payment-hardware volume is actually placed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate ICT- and payment-relevant DNS entries in the NEN Registr DNS, capture admitted-supplier lists, and monitor each DNS for výzvy k podání nabídky rather than relying on top-level notice streams.

coverage_gaps.description: Because each contracting authority chooses its own certified e-tool, full documentation coverage requires a maintained registry mapping banking-relevant authorities (ICO) to their current profil zadavatele host. No such mapping exists yet for this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an ICO→profile-URL table from the VVZ/ISVZ profile-address fields and the ISVZ profile validator; re-verify quarterly since authorities migrate hosts.

coverage_gaps.description: This pass established the platform layer but not the empirical query vocabulary: no systematic enumeration was done of the Czech phrasings actually used in banking/payment tender titles (e.g. akceptace platebních karet, pronájem platebních terminálů, platební brána, zúčtování, bankovní služby vedení účtů, pokladní systém, provozování platebního styku).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a title-corpus pass over NEN and VVZ search results for each candidate phrase, measure hit counts and noise, and freeze a scored keyword list alongside the CPV filters.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal and regional buyers are a major demand pool for card acceptance and terminals (the confirmed Přerov card-acceptance tender is an example), but sub-national authorities are spread across many e-tools and were only sampled here, not mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the authority registry to the 13 kraje, statutory cities and large hospital/utility buyers, and prioritise those with recent payment-acceptance activity.

coverage_gaps.description: English coverage of this cell is thin by nature: NEN offers an /en mirror and TED carries English translations of above-threshold notices, but below-threshold CZ notices and all tender documentation are Czech-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Czech as the primary collection language and use the NEN /en mirror and TED English only for cross-checking and for analyst-facing summaries; budget for machine translation of zadávací dokumentace.

coverage_gaps.description: Rate limits, robots policies and terms of use for NEN, VVZ and the commercial e-tool hosts were not examined in this pass, and the Hlídač státu API's key/quota terms are unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before building collectors, review robots.txt and terms for each host and obtain a Hlídač API token; prefer official bulk open data wherever it substitutes for crawling.

coverage_gaps.description: No authenticated TED API key or tested expert query exists yet for country=CZE crossed with the finance/payments CPV set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register for a TED Developer Portal API key, build and test the CZ expert query against docs.ted.europa.eu/api/latest, and store the query as a versioned artefact.

coverage_gaps.description: The finance/payments CPV pick-list is only partially enumerated (66110000, 66113000, 66172000 confirmed by name; 661/666/72 branches not fully expanded).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extract the full CPV codelist from the eForms SDK and hand-select every 66xxxxxx code plus the 72xxxxxx IT codes CZ buyers use for card, ATM and core-banking systems.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumerated list of CZ contracting authorities most likely to buy banking/payment services (ČNB, ministries, Česká pošta, health insurers, regions, state funds, universities, transport operators) with their IČO identifiers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an IČO-keyed CZ buyer watchlist from TED award history plus ARES/registers, and run buyer-scoped TED queries alongside CPV-scoped ones to catch mis-coded notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Utilities-sector (Directive 2014/25) and defence/security notices naming CZ entities were not separately examined, nor were contract-modification notices, which reveal extensions of incumbent banking contracts without re-tender.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add notice-type filters for modification and utilities forms to the CZ query set; modifications are the strongest signal of incumbent lock-in.

coverage_gaps.description: The cross-border dimension of the cell — non-CZ suppliers winning CZ notices, and CZ suppliers winning notices elsewhere — has no retrieval design yet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: After the CZ baseline exists, invert the query: search TED award notices EU-wide for winners with CZ registered addresses, and for CZ buyers awarding to foreign winners.

coverage_gaps.description: ÚOHS (Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže) decisions on challenged CZ procurements were not covered in this pass, though they are the richest narrative source on contested banking/IT awards.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the ÚOHS decision database (sbírky rozhodnutí) in a subsequent cell or extension of this one; it is a high-value indirect source revealing bidder identities and pricing disputes.

coverage_gaps.description: Two candidate URLs (ted.europa.eu/en/simap/cpv, mmr.gov.cz NPO landing page) were inferred from site structure rather than directly observed, and the TED-CSV dataset path is legacy.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route all three through the deterministic liveness pass and replace with observed URLs before they enter production collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional-level oversight bodies were not covered: Ministerstvo financí's financial-control/audit arm over territorial units, krajské úřady audit outputs, and Krajský soud v Brně (first-instance reviewer of ÚOHS procurement decisions, below NSS).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass on Krajský soud v Brně judgments (justice.cz / infosoud) and MF public-finance-control reports; Krajský soud is the missing middle tier between ÚOHS and NSS.

coverage_gaps.description: The CZ glossary built here is strong on procurement-procedure terms but thin on payments-domain tender vocabulary (e.g. akceptace platebních karet, platební terminály, bankomaty, kartové centrum, zpracování transakcí, jádrový bankovní systém).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the keyword set with acquiring/terminal/ATM/core-banking Czech terms plus English-in-Czech usage (POS, ATM, acquiring, core banking) and re-run full-text searches over the ÚOHS collection and ISVZ open data.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level regulator/audit layers adjacent to this cell were not scouted: EBA payment institutions register, ECB/SSM lists, European Court of Auditors, and TED/EU procurement remedies — all of which cover CZ entities and cross-border bidders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up cell or extend this one to EBA/ECB registers and ECA reports for cross-border payment actors likely to bid in CZ.

coverage_gaps.description: No assessment was made of publication lag: how long after a decision or audit becomes effective it appears in the ÚOHS collection, the NKÚ Věstník, or JERRS.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During the first collection cycles, measure decision-date vs publication-date deltas per source and record them as freshness metadata.

coverage_gaps.description: Reuse terms were not established for the NGO aggregator (Hlídač státu) or confirmed per-dataset on NKOD.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read Hlídač státu API terms and NKOD per-dataset licence fields before building dependent pipelines; prefer primary regulator sources where licence is unambiguous.

coverage_gaps.description: No mapping yet from financial-sector buyer (ICO) to hosting e-tendering platform beyond ČNB. Without this, platform crawling is untargeted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an ICO→buyer-profile→platform resolution table using the NEN buyer-profile registry and vhodne-uverejneni.cz /profil/{ICO} pages for a defined list of CZ financial-sector public and state-owned buyers.

coverage_gaps.description: Private-sector (commercial bank, fintech, PSP) RFPs are essentially invisible on the public platforms; PROEBIZ/TENDERBOX corporate deployments are the most plausible but unconfirmed route.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate PROEBIZ and Tendersystems customer-reference and case-study pages for named financial-sector corporate clients; check whether any corporate tender boards are publicly readable.

coverage_gaps.description: No assessment yet of machine-access affordances (RSS, JSON endpoints, robots.txt, rate limits, bot defences) for E-ZAK instances, Tenderarena's JSF interface, Josephine, Gemin and PVU.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a technical reconnaissance pass per platform recording feed availability, pagination scheme, robots.txt and ToS on automated access, before committing to a crawler design.

coverage_gaps.description: CEE cross-border mirrors were covered only via Opentender.eu; tenders.guru and any SK/PL regional aggregators sharing the JOSEPHINE/ProeBiz stack were not verified in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on tenders.guru, SK JOSEPHINE/ProeBiz deployments and other CEE mirrors to test cross-border coverage of the same vendor stack.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovak-language querying was not performed, although JOSEPHINE/ProeBiz is a CZ-SK cross-border stack and Slovak terminology ('verejné obstarávanie', 'elektronické trhovisko') would surface additional deployments and documentation.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an sk-language query set in the next pass.

coverage_gaps.description: No structured, automatable feed identified for role changes / executive appointments at CZ commercial banks; candidate aggregators (ManagementNews, EduCity 'Personální změny', MediaGuru) were seen only as search hits and not assessed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicate a follow-up pass to CZ 'personální změny' aggregators and to bank press-room appointment sections; assess feed availability and coverage of IT/payments roles.

coverage_gaps.description: Career pages were captured for KB, ČS, ČSOB and ČNB only. Missing: Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit CZ/SK, Air Bank/PPF, Fio, mBank, Trinity/Creditas, plus acquirers and processors (Global Payments CZ, Worldline, Nexi, ČSOB acquiring) and integrators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a complete registry of career-page and press-room URLs for all CZ banks, acquirers/processors and their integrators before starting collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Startup/tech-specific CZ job boards (StartupJobs.cz, Welcome to the Jungle CZ, Techloop) were not searched; these carry fintech and vendor engineering roles that mainstream boards miss.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over CZ tech job boards with the bilingual keyword list.

coverage_gaps.description: Several conference sources were assessed from search snippets rather than fetched agenda pages; per-edition programme URL patterns (beyond cardforum's /data/cardforumYYYYinfo.pdf) are unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch each event's current programme page to confirm URL patterns and whether speaker lists are public or gated, before scheduling collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side signals (Printec competitors' and partners' own press releases, case studies and award submissions announcing CZ bank wins) were not systematically enumerated in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a vendor press-room registry (terminal makers, processors, core-banking vendors active in CZ) as a mirror-image confirmation channel for partnership/pilot signals.

coverage_gaps.description: No dedicated Czech trade outlet found that covers cards/acquiring/payment-processing as a beat (analogous to a Czech 'PaymentsSource'); payments coverage is scattered across E15, Bankovnictví, Lupa and retail media.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search additionally for Měšec.cz, Peníze.cz, Podnikatel.cz, Finparáda, Fintree/Fintech Cowboys and the SBK (Sdružení pro bankovní karty) newsletter as candidate payments-specific Czech sources in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Industry-association and vendor communication channels (ČBA – Česká bankovní asociace, SBK, ČNB press releases, vendor Czech-language press rooms) were not covered in this cell but are the main disclosure route for private-bank supplier deals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up cell to association/vendor PR channels; cross-link them to this media cell for corroboration.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Czech banking/payments tenders was not located as a distinct source; searches surfaced only Czech-language outlets plus generic international pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check Czech Radio International, Expats.cz, CEE-focused outlets (Emerging Europe, IntelliNews, CEE Legal Matters) for English secondary coverage of Czech bank/payments deals.

coverage_gaps.description: Retrieval depth of outlet archives (how far back article indexes and RSS reach, whether HN's archiv.hn.cz is fully open) was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a sitemap/archive-depth probe per outlet before designing the historical backfill; consider Anopress/Newton Media (Czech press databases) for licensed retrospective full-text.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional coverage of municipal/transport-authority ticketing and payment tenders is represented only by Zdopravy.cz and Deník.cz; regional dailies and transport-authority newsrooms are not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate regional Deník mutations and city/transport-company press rooms (DPP, DPMB, DPO, ROPID, IDSK) as a secondary tier for ticketing/EMV tenders.

coverage_gaps.description: The Czech national web archive (Webarchiv, operated by the National Library of the Czech Republic) was not searched or assessed in this slice, despite being the most likely holder of deep historic captures of .cz government and supplier sites.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated cs pass on 'Webarchiv Národní knihovny ČR', 'webarchiv.cz sklizeň', 'archivace webu veřejná správa' and assess its search/API access and whether captures are publicly retrievable or reading-room-only.

coverage_gaps.description: For several key structured routes — VVZ/cdz.vvz.nipez.cz distribution, the NIPEZ Registr veřejných zakázek consumer interface, and the ISVZ OpenData download paths — I identified the systems but did not establish exact endpoint URLs, schema versions or authentication requirements.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch portal-vz.cz's profil zadavatele XML/XSD documentation and the NIPEZ service-usage rules, then record concrete endpoint URLs, schema versions (incl. Vyhláška 345/2023 Sb. forms) and any registration requirement in the source register.

coverage_gaps.description: The contracting-authority side is mapped only for ČNB. The wider CZ banking/payments buyer set — commercial banks that are not public contracting authorities, Národní rozvojová banka, Česká pošta, state institutions with card/terminal estates — has not been resolved to profile URLs or IČOs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an IČO-keyed buyer list via ARES, then resolve each to its profil zadavatele (NEN or commercial platform) and record the per-buyer structured collection route; note explicitly which buyers are outside the procurement act and therefore invisible in these datasets.

coverage_gaps.description: No source found in this slice directly exposes contract END dates as a queryable field; expiry must be derived from Registr smluv contract metadata (effective date plus stated duration) or from framework-agreement terms in tender documentation.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prototype an expiry-derivation rule over Registr smluv XML for a sample of financial-sector buyers and measure what share of contracts yield a usable end date; document the residual blind spot.

coverage_gaps.description: The Registr smluv publisher explicitly warns that its dataset contains personal data and that the recipient becomes a GDPR controller. No handling policy has been defined for this slice's recommended bulk ingestion.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a minimisation and retention policy before ingesting ISRS dumps: drop natural-person counterparties and signatory names at parse time, retain only legal-entity records, and document the lawful basis for the remainder.

coverage_gaps.description: Certified Czech e-procurement platforms other than NEN — Tender arena, E-ZAK instances beyond ČNB, Gemin, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz — were identified only in passing; their statutory XML profile-export endpoints were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each certified electronic tool, locate its standard profile XML export URL pattern and record one worked example, so that any buyer can be collected structurally once its platform is known.

coverage_gaps.description: DORA requires financial entities to maintain a register of information on all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers, reported to competent authorities; CSRD/ESRS requires value-chain disclosure. Neither the group-level nor the ČNB-facing manifestation of these obligations was investigated in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether ČNB, the ESAs or the groups themselves publish or summarise any part of the DORA register of information, and mine group annual reports / sustainability statements of Erste, KBC, SG, UniCredit and RBI for named ICT third-party providers and outsourcing concentration disclosures covering Czech operations.

coverage_gaps.description: Cell coverage is uneven across the five groups: Erste and SG are well mapped, KBC and RBI are covered at policy level only, and UniCredit's current procurement owner is unresolved. Second-tier CEE parents with Czech exposure (e.g. other foreign-owned CZ banks and their group sourcing arms) were not addressed at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass per group on: current procurement entity, portal endpoint, category organisation, and named CZ contracting entity. Then extend the actor list beyond the five named groups to all foreign-parented CZ banks.

coverage_gaps.description: No aggregator or archival layer was located for group sourcing: no supplier-network discovery surface (e.g. Ariba Discovery), no procurement-tender aggregator covering private bank buyers in CEE, and no systematic use of web archives to recover withdrawn supplier pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate commercial supplier-network discovery surfaces and CEE tender aggregators for private-sector bank demand; and set up Wayback-based monitoring of the identified supplier/procurement pages so withdrawn registration rules and superseded policy versions remain recoverable.

coverage_gaps.description: German (Vienna: Erste, RBI), Dutch (Brussels: KBC) and Italian (Milan: UniCredit) are the working languages of three of the five decision centres, and none was searched. Only cs, en and incidental fr were used.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add de, nl and it query sets (Einkauf/Beschaffung/Lieferantenportal; aankoop/inkoop/leveranciers; acquisti/fornitori/albo fornitori) — group procurement pages and job ads are frequently richer in the HQ language than in English.

coverage_gaps.description: Hiring and organisational signals (group procurement job ads naming categories, tools and locations; CZ-based sourcing roles at group entities) were identified as a route but never systematically collected, partly because the richest surface (LinkedIn) is login-gated and ToS-restricted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use the groups' own career sites (erstegroup.com careers, erstedigital.com, rbinternational.com, kbc.com, societegenerale.com) rather than LinkedIn, filtering for procurement/sourcing/vendor-management roles located in Prague or covering the Czech market. Fully compliant and unrestricted.

coverage_gaps.description: Several URLs in this slice were obtained from search-result listings rather than fetched directly (KBC our-suppliers, SG Sourcing Hub, RBI code-of-conduct PDFs, Erste Digital, the smlouvy.gov.cz example PDF). Only the Erste Group Procurement page and kb.cz/cs/dodavatele were actually retrieved and read.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route all candidates through the deterministic liveness/verification pass before they enter the source register; treat unretrieved URLs as unverified rather than dead if they fail once.

coverage_gaps.description: Ministry of the Interior (MV ČR) and Digitální a informační agentura (DIA) are the actual administrators of the public-administration payment-gateway DNS and of gov.cz portal services, but sit outside this cell's named actor list.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign MV ČR and DIA buyer profiles (including the payment-gateway DNS on NEN) to a cell explicitly, or extend this cell to cover them.

coverage_gaps.description: Central-state buyers are split across at least four e-procurement platforms — E-ZAK (MF, ČNB), NEN/NIPEZ, TENDER ARENA (Česká pošta), and commercial profiles such as vhodne-uverejneni/Gemin — with no single crawl covering all document-level content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-platform adapter set keyed on buyer IČO, with ISVZ open data as the reconciliation spine to detect notices no adapter caught.

coverage_gaps.description: ISVZ open data changed format in February 2024 (legacy XML before, new datasets after), and older agency tenders (e.g. the 2017 customs terminal contract) are reachable mainly as loose PDFs on agency sites.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ingest both the legacy and new open-data series and schema-map them; supplement pre-2024 gaps with targeted agency-site PDF crawls.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code shortlist was established for state purchases of card acceptance, payment gateways, POS terminals and payment-system integration, so open-data filtering is currently keyword-only and will over- and under-match.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the CPV set empirically from the customs terminals tender, MF gateway contracts and TED CZ notices, then use CPV + keyword in combination.

coverage_gaps.description: Hlídač státu offers full data and an API but points commercial users to a licensing contact; reuse terms for commercial market intelligence were not established in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Clarify licence terms before any bulk or productised use, and keep the pipeline's evidential layer on the state-published open data (registr smluv, ISVZ, TED).

coverage_gaps.description: Only a subset of the 13 kraje + Praha were located concretely (MSK, Karlovarský, Jihomoravský, Plzeňský central purchasing). Středočeský, Ústecký, Liberecký, Královéhradecký, Pardubický, Vysočina, Jihočeský, Olomoucký, Zlínský regional profiles were not individually pinned down.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve all 14 regional buyer profile URLs directly from the VVZ profile registry by ICO, then apply the generic E-ZAK/NEN parsers.

coverage_gaps.description: Statutární města beyond Prague/Brno (Ostrava, Plzeň, Liberec, Olomouc, Hradec Králové, Pardubice, České Budějovice, Ústí nad Labem, Zlín, Havířov, Karviná, Most, Opava, Jihlava, Teplice, Chomutov, Frýdek-Místek, Děčín, Karlovy Vary, Mladá Boleslav, Přerov, Prostějov) were only reached via aggregator listings, not their own profiles.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a fixed roster of the 26 statutární města plus their transport companies (DPO, PMDP, DPMLJ, DPMO, DPMHK, DPMP...) and resolve each to a profile URL.

coverage_gaps.description: School canteen payments, waste-fee and local-fee (místní poplatky) cashless collection, and municipal POS acceptance for counters (podatelna/pokladna) were part of the cell rationale but produced no concrete tender sources in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted cs queries: 'zakázka stravovací systém školní jídelna bezhotovostní platba', 'platební terminál na pokladně městského úřadu zakázka', 'poplatek za odpad platba kartou obec'; also CPV-filter 66100000 and 30140000 in NEN/VVZ.

coverage_gaps.description: Prague městské části: only Praha 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, 19 were observed; the full set of 57 (22 administrative) districts is unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate all MČ Praha ICOs from the state registry and resolve each to its profile via VVZ.

coverage_gaps.description: No robots.txt / rate-limit / ToS assessment was performed for the commercial platform families (Tender arena, e-zakazky.cz, vhodne-uverejneni.cz, profilzadavatele.cz) that host most municipal profiles.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before scaling collection, check robots.txt and terms for each platform family and prefer official open-data channels (Prague open data, Registr smluv dumps, Hlídač API) where they duplicate the same content.
